does: Brings out the taste of a dish with salt, and balances it with pepper, acid or fat.
how: Salt in small steps as the dish cooks, not only at the end.
Taste before serving, from a clean spoon.
Add a little salt if the dish tastes flat, and a few drops of acid if it tastes dull or heavy.
Stir, wait a moment and taste again.

cues.text: The dish tastes more of itself and not of salt. It is bright, and nothing sticks out.

mistakes.mistake: Salting a liquid fully before it has boiled down, so that it ends up too salty.
mistakes.fix: Salt lightly anything that will reduce, and correct it at the end.
Taste every time. No amount on paper replaces it.
